sources.title: Aatrox Build Guide: [26.4] Fundamentals Of Aatrox // Season 16 Guide

passive.name: Deathbringer Stance
passive.text: Periodically, Aatrox's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage and heals him, based on the target's max health.

spells.name: The Darkin Blade
spells.text: Aatrox slams his greatsword down, dealing physical damage. He can swing three times, each with a different area of effect.

spells.name: Infernal Chains
spells.text: Aatrox smashes the ground, dealing damage to the first enemy hit. Champions and large monsters have to leave the impact area quickly or they will be dragged to the center and take the damage again.

spells.name: Umbral Dash
spells.text: Passively, Aatrox heals when damaging enemy champions. On activation, he dashes in a direction.

spells.name: World Ender
spells.text: Aatrox unleashes his demonic form, fearing nearby enemy minions and gaining attack damage, increased healing, and Move Speed. If he gets a takedown, this effect is extended.

damage.value: Aatrox deals sustained physical damage with his three Q swings and periodic bonus magic damage with his passive attack.

archetype.value: Aatrox is a bruiser who relies on omnivamp and combos to fight in duels and teamfights.

winCondition.value: Aatrox wins by using his mid-game strength to further his lead.

spikes.why: Aatrox reaches early powerspikes at these levels, so preserving HP beforehand matters.
Aatrox reaches his biggest powerspike and dominates during mid game.

spikes.at: When Aatrox lands Q sweet spots
spikes.why: Aatrox reduces his passive cooldown, giving him more opportunities for bonus damage and healing.

bait.why: After Aatrox spends Infernal Chains, its damage and potential pull are unavailable until its cooldown ends.

mistakes.value: Aatrox players risk losing HP by taking high-risk trades early.
Aatrox makes a mistake by treating his strong sustain as if it makes him unkillable.
